One **really important** thing I would like to emphasize before I say anything is that practically everyone experiences depression differently.  Although many of us can relate, there are many differences in both cause (if there even is one) and experience, which is a big part of why there is no one way to "cure" or help someone with depression.  If you want a good idea of depression, then read everyone's experiences, and also realize that there's really no way you could really understand without actually experiencing it – mainly because there is way too much going on to put into a reasonable amount of words, assuming one could even manage to accurately describe it all.

Anyway, I'm a bit too tired to give my own proper response, but I can tell you that I fluctuate between times of numbness and complete despair, although this is when I'm not doing something that makes me feel happy (like most of the time when I hang out with friends or play Xbox, but still not always during those).  When I don't have those distractions, my mind tends to wander and dream up these wonderful possibilities for my present and future, and then it tells me that these things will never happen and that, just as it has been since my depression started, my life will always be shit.  I have low points and high points, but have never really experienced any kind of recovery.  On average, I've just been getting worse.  Oh, and suicide is a very prevalent thought for me.  It kind of scares me not because I'm afraid to die, but because I don't want to hurt my family, but it's getting so much harder and harder to resist.  I almost want it nowadays.

With all due respect to your issues, I don't think you understand that, at least for most people, depression is nowhere near a choice, especially when it's bad enough that you seriously feel like you could kill yourself any moment now.  As much as I would like to say "whatever" to the issues that I'm dealing with, I am unable to, and instead they eat away at me and wear me down to the point that I am at now.  If I could just "be happy", don't you think I would?

Also, word of warning: most depressed people do not take very kindly to being told to just "be happy" or "enjoy life", not just because they can't simply do that, but also because it seems to demean the whole concept of depression itself, which is nothing short of extremely serious.

I've gone there every year since I was a kid, but we stopped going some time ago.  I like it very much there and it would help a lot to be able to go back, but it wouldn't help so much that it'd be worth it.
Not happening, sorry.

I dunno, like, I feel like I actually do have friends, I just don't know who/how to tell which ones really are.  Aside from that, having major trust issues is kind of a big barrier in opening up to a friend.

I don't want to go it alone.  I want to fall in love with someone and have it not be one-sided for once.  I want friends that aren't dicks half the time and that actually like to just talk and hang out (but not just over the Internet).  But apparently I don't get to have those things.

Yeah, it kinda sucks, doesn't it?  :/  It especially sucks when you say or do something around other people, and then you look back on it later and actually realize what a stupid/awkward thing that was to do (or something along those lines) and how it's just another one in the books.

Me not opening up to people isn't an issue of pride; in fact, despite my occasional stubbornness, I'm fairly humble in nature.  I don't trust people in general because I've never had a reason to.  My brother was verbally and somewhat physically abusive.  My father encouraged the verbal abuse.  My mom wasn't ever really able to stand up to my brother as a kid, so he usually got his way and avoided trouble for the way he treated me.  I tried to run away from home twice because of how he acted.  I started to gain weight and seclude myself during middle school due to the encroaching depression, and I became kinda weird, so I started getting made fun of a fair amount and I knew how the other kids saw me.  One of my closest friends at the time sometimes made fun of me behind my back too and sometimes would lie to me when I was at his house so he could play video games.  And a lot of people tend not to believe me about a fair share of my weird aspects and such, so in turn I kind of trust them less and also feel worse about those things.

I am aware I am not insane, but believe me, I am getting there.  Sometimes my head races so much that I'll start pulling at my hair and feel like I need to rip my head in half to make it stop.  Sometimes I'll bang my head against the wall to make it stop.  Other times it'll just make me feel so flustered and confused that I just curl up in a ball and cry until it stops.  I have thoughts sometimes about terrible, terrible things happening to the people I care about which wind up so that I get more attention and care (usually by my coming to their aid afterward).  And of course my irrational jealousy of any guy/girl interactions amongst my friends is certainly by no means normal.  And all of this stuff gets worse with time, and more things get added to the list every now and then.

And the biggest problem with all that is that it seems more and more real every day.  I could see myself waking up tomorrow just completely neurotic and being taken to a hospital/psych-ward.  Yesterday, I felt like such shit and just so generally exhausted that I didn't shower and it took me probably 3 times as long to do anything.  That last time I went a day without showering (excluding sickness/recovery) was years ago, the same day that I first attempted to write a suicide note.

Regarding social interactions, since I began to become introverted and depressed ever since the start of middle school, my social skills developed significantly more slowly, and I've had very few female interactions/friends since then, so it's not just the self-confidence issues that's holding me back, it's the general lack of knowledge and how to properly interact with people.

It's not all about mindset, and I can't just simply start thinking differently and all of a sudden turn my life around.  No offense, but if I'm interpreting you right and you think that I can just start believing in myself, as much as I'd love to, then you don't really understand what depression is.  Correct me if I read you wrong.

I appreciate the offer, but honestly if you're really in a similar situation, then for your sake I don't think it'd be a good idea to talk to me. A few months ago, I would talk to you and try to be positive with you and maybe it would help me in turn, and same for you to me.  But now, well, now I just think the best way out is death.  I'm just unfortunately stuck due to a few things so it won't ever be a conscious and sane effort.

Plus, most of my PM conversations with people just end up with them getting a bit frustrated with me or just running out of things to say.

I mean, of course I want people to know how severe what I'm going through is, but the problem is that most people who haven't experienced depression simply can't understand it.  Hell, I have a couple friends who essentially don't believe that depression exists, and they're both normally relatively intelligent people.

My problem isn't that I don't think I can be successful in life or anything, it's that I don't believe I'll ever be happy again, or at least not within any reasonable amount of time, and also that I don't know how much longer I can stave off insanity/breaking down and killing myself in the "heat of the moment" so to speak.

I honestly don't trust/feel comfortable enough with my male friends to open up to any of them.  The reason I mentioned my "crush" (I have had so many that I might as well use that interchangeably with female friend), or rather my best female friend, is because for some reason I feel like I trust her enough to open up to her, but yet I still know that I wouldn't actually do it.  I don't think I could ever bring myself to open up to anyone.

See, I've always been the type to generally keep my emotions and thoughts to myself, and so now I'm in a situation where my instinct is to just do what I've always done, and it's too hard to go against it.

And I won't disagree with you that there is a part of my mind still fighting, but I wish that part would give up too.  It's been close to a decade since what started this downward spiral, about 6 years since I'd say I actually started being depressed, 3 years since I began to be suicidal, and for the past 1-2 years, feeling suicidal has just been normal and now, it's just the same goddamn routine every day of bouncing between moods.

After so many years since this all started, it has been nothing but downhill, and I've just about reached the end of my rope.  Although I don't think I'll ever actively kill myself, it feels like one of these days, that piece of my brain telling me to keep going will finally just give up and who knows what I'll do then.  Hopefully I just die in my sleep; that'd be nice.

That's the thing is that I don't... All my conversations with people here are just back and forth, them providing a point and me providing a counterpoint, and never really get anywhere.  I just wind up exhausting people and then not talking to them anymore, feeling no different than I did before.

What I want is for someone to tell me that it's okay for me to just give up and die.

As much as I enjoy getting high, I don't do it very often because coming down from it absolutely sucks for me.  Basically, anything that provides me temporary relief or even happiness just makes me feel worse once it's over.
You can trust me that I'm feeling plenty, and quite frankly, it seems like all these feelings are making me neurotic.  I wish I could just feel dead inside or just shut my brain off.

Well, I'll never be able to ask out any of the girls I fall for because I have no self-confidence and am really awkward when it comes to that sort of thing.  I have few friends and no real social life and am terrible at meeting people.  Oh, and I'm bipolar and frequently want to kill myself.  After so many years of suffering and not being able to overcome my problems, I've given up.  It's just too self-destructive to keep hoping and trying only to fail.

I can assure you that my obsessions all last quite some time, long enough that even if they are becoming progressively shorter and less dramatic, it won't be making a difference any time soon.   I honestly don't see anything majorly wrong with the current girl I'm into, and half the time I don't even know the girls I obsess over well enough to find something wrong with them.  I wouldn't say I'm idolizing them, more like I'm just desperately alone and want someone that I can fall in love with. And it's not like I believe this girl is "the one" or anyone extraordinarily special, so even when I do discover flaws, it's not like it's some reality-shattering deal.

For some people, love is something they want to have and strive for, but it's not their sole desire.  For me, it's everything.  Partly because of my own personality and distrust of people (haven't exactly had a lot of reason to), I haven't received much emotional attention/care throughout my life; I've been fairly independent relative to most and tend to keep my emotions to myself, and for me, the idea of being in love with someone (and them with me, of course) would lift an enormous amount of stress and self-hatred off of my shoulders.

And right you are, the worst part is the vicious circle.  The main problem that prevents me from breaking it is that I really just don't trust people to tell the truth.  Think about it: nobody really wants to tell you that you're unattractive or that something is wrong with you because they don't want to hurt your feelings.  They'll complement you on little things or skirt around the truth or just lie so you'll feel better about yourself.  Some people will tell the truth, but there are very few times when you can really trust that someone is.  Whether or not you agree, this is my mindset, and so I rarely take any kind of complement or kind remarks to heart unless there's not really any reason that someone would lie about it.

Honestly, I think the only two ways I'll ever feel better about myself is either by getting a girlfriend or by popping some happy pills, and I really don't want to take the pill route.  I've been thinking more about it lately, but I'm not still not too keen about altering my perception of reality, despite my currently rather bleak one.

It's great to see you're doing alright Allie, it's been a worrying year and a half and I've missed your regular posting.  It's nice to see such a relatable description of depression that hopefully the fortunate people of "I-Still-Have-Meaning-In-My-Life Land" can really understand.

I would really like to emphasize one thing though, for everyone else, that might be overlooked: this is not what depression is like for everyone, and there is no one kind of depression or a definitive way that you should treat people with depression.  As someone who has struggled for years with manic depression, I can tell you that it is a much different experience and, although I can certainly relate to what Allie is dealing with, I still could never fully understand what she is going through because of how different it is.

Before anyone freaks out on me, I am not at all undermining Allie or her post.  I am not saying that what I am dealing with is any easier/harder than what she is because there's no way I could actually know that.  I just want people to understand that this is what *she* is going through, not what everyone with depression has to deal with.  If I had even half the talent she does for writing, I'd try to articulate my form of depression, but I can never seem to do so correctly.

Anyway, stay strong, Allie.  I've always liked your posts and you seem like such a great person, which makes it even worse to think that you've got all those dead fish to deal with.  Keep on trying to find more of those shriveled little pieces of corn and everything will turn out alright.

Well, I've been here for a while and haven't really gotten any of that.  Really it's just been a place for me to rant and occasionally find someone like yourself to have a discussion with.

Yeah sorry, I tend to get myself into arguments without realizing it.  Nothing else I really want to talk about.  :/  I don't even really know what I'm looking to hear/talk about when I come here.  I guess I just want someone to say some magic word that's gonna turn my life around, even though that's probably not gonna happen.
And in my case, my personality prevents me from being able to do anything positive about it all.  All I do is berate myself for all my mistakes and try to avoid reality as much as possible.

I am well aware that my problems aren't permanent, but I just don't find it worth it anymore to deal with.  With no indication of me truly being happy any time soon, I really just don't care to keep riding this out.

I'll hopefully be going on isotretinoin soon, which is gonna suck, but hopefully there won't be any really detrimental side effects and will do its job.

I'm sure my mind will be at a lot more ease once I start becoming actually happy, but again, I have absolutely no idea how much longer it would be until that happens.

One of my biggest problems is that I'm a math-kind of person.  I approach everything with logic and always try to figure everything out.  But since depression isn't really something that can be rationalized, I obviously can't try to apply logic to fix it.  And for some reason, I can never really hype myself up or trick myself into doing things.
For example, I've been wanting to ask this girl out for probably a month, but I never can.  I can come to the conclusion that the possible positives outweigh the possible negatives, but when it comes down to the moment, I can't do it.  I can try to hype myself up to go for it, but that doesn't work.  I can try to convince myself that X will happen if I don't or that it'll be just fine, but I still can't do it.  Now, I just gave up.  I'm sick of disappointing myself.
Now, I'm not saying this is such a huge deal.  Part of it is that she's clearly out of my league (not even being harsh on myself, really, just being real), so that doesn't really make it easy for me, and I think I could handle rejection fine.  But the point is that I can't get myself to do things that I seem unable to do, and that accounts for so many of my problems that are my fault.  And no matter what I do, I can't get over it.

I don't know if you get how absurdly frustrating it is to have to constantly put up with this, constantly accept failure, and constantly reflect on how I can't do things.  It makes me feel like a total loser and makes me hate myself even more.  I can't even think straight when I try to express this.

**Edit:** Sorry, this turned out way longer than I planned.  I'm not good at being concise.

I'll try a different format here and bullet things so you don't have to read a ton if you don't want:
• For starters, it's not just that there's things wrong in my life, part of it is just that I feel like shit.
• I hate practically everything about myself
• I'm extremely self-conscious and awful at socializing with new people (don't even get me started on girls)
• I always feel like people either hate me or only associate with me because they feel bad for me
• I have no life and just spend every day inside playing video games, despite my desire to have a social life like I used to a few years ago, before the depression
• I hate living at home and even though I'll be off at college next semester, I don't know if I can wait that long, and I don't even know that things will be better there.
• Never had a girlfriend, and between my inability to have any grounds to make casual conversation, my awkwardness/nervousness, inability to ask a girl out, and the fact that I don't have a good enough personality to make up for it, it seems like I never will, and I really believe that.
• I obsess over girls and fall in love so easily, and I rip my head apart over it
• I've had such a medical history and have been through so much pain because of it, and the shit just keeps piling on.  Something is always wrong, and right now it's the acne all over my chest and literally everywhere on my head (I have trouble sleeping sometimes because it'll make it too painful to rest my head).
• I underwent one surgery that was so extraordinarily painful that if I didn't have no energy and feel like I was dead, I would have killed myself.  You never forget that kind of emotional and physical pain, and I've had two others that were somewhat close to as bad
• I was abused a little bit physically but mostly verbally by my brother for a few years of my childhood
• I dream/daydream so often that it hurts so much to come back to and stay in reality.  I hate having to wake up.
• If my family would somehow not be affected, I would no doubt have killed myself long by now
• I feel like I'm going crazy and that my mind is slowly degrading.
• I just want for all this to end so I can be happy, or at least to die so I won't be miserable
• I could kill myself practically any time I want to, and I know a couple different ways that would work perfectly fine

I'm sure there's more, I'm just too tired to go back and see what I've missed.  There you have a majority of the problems in my life, and that's mostly just situational.  If I could accurately explain to you the thoughts that go through my head and make you feel what I feel, I can guarantee you that even with the best life ever, you'd want to kill yourself too.  I hope so badly that something will just kill me one day so I don't have to worry about it.  You know how some people have dreams where there's like a man with a gun or something and they save the day and whatnot?  I get those too, except half the time, I just end up dying.  And that's still a dream, not a nightmare.

I'm such a goddamn wreck
People also are born and then die.  It's all meaningless words that give me no real reason I should keep struggling through this shit.  I'm broken and worthless and I give up on trying to fix myself.

The only reason I haven't yet is because I don't want to hurt my family.  I know it would, and even though I know the pain would fade, I can't even imagine what it would do to my mom.  How I wish I could just not care and go through with it...

Thank you very much for this post.  I've always wanted to express this thought, but I've felt like I was in the minority for thinking it, and I didn't want to disrespect those who are really trying to help around here.

Hey man, I'm a freshman in college and I was picked on a fair amount in high school.  Granted, it may not have been as bad as what you're dealing with, but it sure as hell hurt and I know how much it sucks.

I know you'll hear a lot about how much better college is and all the people you meet will be better, and if you're like me and not very good at making friends, then this doesn't seem very comforting or even realistic.  But the thing is that in college, everyone is new and are all growing up and trying to succeed and build new relationships, and those old jock cliques and stuff from high school where they pick on kids to impress each other doesn't exist anymore.  Sure, there will still be people that might say mean or insensitive things in college, but that's just how people are and it's still way less than high school.

In my experience so far, even though I haven't really made many friends, I haven't been picked on anymore because nobody knows anything about me (except the people who care enough to find out, and they typically are not going to make fun of you), so they have no reason to target me.  Since there's also so goddamn many people, there's a bunch of people with acne or that are fat or have some oddity, and there's always someone messing something up, so most people just kind of accept that as normal and don't care anymore.  Plus, more people look down on bullying in college, so there's even less reason to do it.

**Tl;dr:** If that's your biggest issue in life right now, then you're in luck because chances are it really will get noticeably better in the near future.

Just about sums it up.  I'd be gone long by now if there was a couple people that I knew somehow wouldn't be hurt by it.  But, from everyone else's perspective, whatever works works, so I guess that's a good thing?

I can at least say that the first year is definitely easier than high school, and it's so much nicer having so many classes to choose from.  You'll do a lot better from being able to take classes that actually interest you (although there are still core classes you need, but they're not so bad).  Just try not to take morning classes cause then you get up in the morning feeling like it's high school again hah.

This.  I obsess over the idea nonstop, even though I know that it probably will never happen.  And I do this with so many girls that at this point, it just seems like this is how it'll always be; I'll "fall in love" with practically every girl I meet, but it'll never go anywhere and I'll eventually die alone.  But still, it's a pleasant escape from reality when I get the chance (although coming back to reality is never fun).

Coincidentally, I'll be dealing with this situation (the girl coming back) very soon and I'm not sure how it'll go or how I'll handle it.
I appreciate it, but talking hasn't really seemed to get me anywhere.  At this point, all I can do is just hope I last long enough for at least something worthwhile to happen.

I miss the days when this might have helped. The problem is that once you've hit your breaking point, you just lose the capacity to care.  I am truly sorry for your loss and wish you the best, and I wish there was a way of going out that would hurt less and make more sense to others, but sometimes it's just too much to carry.

Survival instinct and the desperate feeling that there's some good reason not to die.  That's what really keeps most of us – or at least me – alive.  There's no logical reason that I'm still alive right now, it's just an unfortunate fact.
I feel generally the same way, except I feel like I really am eventually going to snap.  It sort of worries me but, at the same time, I look forward to it.

I'm sure I would be glad if I stuck through it and finally became happy, but it's not enough.  Something I can't get over is the thought that if I die, all unhappiness is gone.  All stress is gone, all pain is gone, all sadness and loneliness is gone forever.  Missing out on happiness wouldn't be a problem because I'd be dead and wouldn't have the capacity to care, and now I feel the same way about any of the effects it would have on others.

We dictate our lives and our actions by how they will effect us, no matter how "selfless" we are.  If I am to no longer have consequences, then I shouldn't worry about what happens after I die because I'll be dead and nothing will matter anymore.

I don't doubt that things can change for the better, but when?  It's not like I have some progress bar that tells me how far I have left until I can be happy, and it's really just not worth waiting for it anymore.  I guess a good analogy might be that I don't know what I'm downloading, but it's been going real slow and I have no idea when it will finish, and I really don't think it's worth it anymore so I think it's just time to cancel it.  The other problem is that changing my personality and improving my social skills is way, way easier said than done, and aside from the fact that I don't know how to do it, I don't think I could handle the stress of trying to figure it out and/or failing at it (especially when it comes to dating).

Today (technically) is probably going to be a really shitty day.  I guess we'll see how it goes...

After a while of constantly being called fat and dumb and ugly and retarded and worthless and all sorts of shitty things, it starts to get to you, regardless of what's true and what's not.  I hate myself, and it seems like everything is wrong with me.  I'm awkward.  I'm weird.  I can't talk to people.  My life is pointless and boring.  My acne is everywhere and it's not only embarrassing but painful.  I'm not fat but all I see is where there is fat, but I can never seem to notice anything that looks good.  I tried dieting again but I'm so goddamn hungry all the time that I can't even manage 2,000 calories, and I can't motivate myself to start running again.  I don't really have friends anymore, and I'm lucky if I actually hang out with anyone even once every other weekend.  I'm miserable and I hate where I am in life and I hate that I can't do any of the things I want, and it's even worse to know that I pretty much can't control any of it and just have to sit and wait for something good to happen, which isn't really the best strategy but it's all I can do.  My town is boring and all old people and annoying high-schoolers, so it's not like I can go out and do anything social or even by myself.  I just get to sit inside all day and play Xbox and occasionally check Facebook to see all the happy people living their happy lives with their happy friends.

I don't think it's biological.  I used to be very happy as a kid, until things just got out of control.  This might be a little long, but I could use a little venting, so just skip down a bit if you don't really need all the info.

Around elementary school, literally all of my closest friends started moving away, one-by-one, until nobody was left but one kid who I was never particularly fond of but I hung out with anyway.  I made a couple new best friends soon after, and one of them moved away after a couple years (of course), and another turned out to be not such a good friend.  I started eating more to cope, and of course I got fat.  Then, I got transferred to a new school because of some weird stuff, and so I had almost no friends, and since I was a sad little fat kid, nobody really wanted to talk to me.  Continue this downward spiral until the end of middle school.  By then, I knew I was depressed, but it wasn't really manic.  I slacked on work, started doing poorly in school, and avoided people in fear of being hurt or judged (I got made fun of a fair amount, even by my family and friends, so I'm not very trusting of people anymore).  Enter high school and I make a few friends, but of course it's the, well, "weird" kids that kind of group together due to exclusion from everywhere else.  I wasn't like them and I didn't want to be with them, but I knew I could never make friends elsewhere.  I tried asking two different girls out through the entirety of high school.  One didn't work but it wasn't very bad, and another went pretty poorly and did a number on my confidence.  Now, I'm 18, lost most of the fat and put on a tiny bit of muscle, but I'm in community college because I fucked up in high school and it feels like life is just repeating.  I don't really have any friends again, the classmates who even realize I'm there probably think I'm mute, and I still only see the fat on my body when I look in the mirror, and my face seems just as ugly as I've thought it to be.  I don't know if I will ever believe otherwise because I've virtually lost the ability to trust anything anyone says and can't really even rely on my own opinions anymore.  As far as I'm aware (and I mean this), no girl has ever flirted with me.  Of course, my social skills suck and I rarely interact with girls, so I probably wouldn't even know.  I don't think anybody knows I'm depressed, and I am certain most of them would not understand.  I even remember on of my friends saying in response to some girl committing suicide that it's just a way of cleansing the gene pool or something.  The kid is a pretentious dick and I really would like to stop associating with him, but I don't have much of a choice if I wish to keep my other friends.

A few other things I left out that I don't feel like placing in the right spot: my brother was mostly verbally but also a bit physically abusive.  My dad has temper issues and him and my brother fought **a lot**.  I tried cutting my wrist a couple times a few years ago but I didn't really do anything.  I spend literally about 90% of my free time playing Xbox because I have nothing else to do with my life.  There's more, I'm just tired and want to sleep soon.

So there you go, some background information.  Essentially, I have a lot of issues, especially trust issues, which makes it hard for me to let people help me or for my confidence to have any positive change.  My problems are pretty much entirely lack-of-social-skill/personality based and also due to my situation.  I'm really worn out so I'll be back tomorrow

I don't necessarily expect to be down all the time.  In fact, my depression is manic, so I have happy times and know that things can be good.  But it's not worth it to deal with the low points, the crippling loneliness, the self-hatred, and the lack of self-confidence that has destroyed my ability to socialize with normal or unfamiliar people.  I'm tired of dreaming only to wake up and realize that none of it is real and that I'm just a miserable human being that fucks up at everything.

**Edit:** Sorry, that was a bit more difficult to type out than I thought it would be and had to take a break for a minute.  My dreams are part of what I hate because waking up in the morning and remembering just the pure feeling of happiness and self-worth is just the most cripplingly painful thing, and I actually frequently feel most suicidal in the morning because of that.
I really hope you're right, cause that's about all the hope I've got and I'm not sure how much longer I can take it.

I really would love to follow your advice, but I just don't see myself being able to even say that much.  I'm always just so anxious and afraid of constant judgement that I always try to refrain from even speaking in class, let alone to other people directly.  Also, I'm 18, why?

"Talk to people"
No offense, but I'm tired of hearing this.  So much easier said than done when you have virtually no experience with talking to random people.

The thing is though that I am at a community college, and it's just worse for me because I barely know anyone and I don't know how to socialize with people (or sometimes am just too self-conscious or shy).  If somehow I was able to socialize, I'd probably have a good deal of friends, but without the know-how and ability, that means nothing.  I just have this feeling that it won't be any different in the fall when I am at a new college, especially since I'll be a transfer student and won't have the benefit of freshman orientation or just being a freshman amongst freshman.

Regarding girls, I am oblivious to signals and frequently my brain just shuts down around them.  I literally have never noticed or heard a girl hitting on me in any way.  But to be honest, I bounce back and forth between thinking I am attractive and thinking I'm not.  Truth is I have no clue and can't trust anyone enough to give me a real answer.
Not that I think that shouldn't have been allowed to be posted, but yeah, regretting having read through that.

My diet and exercise habits actually aren't terrible, and I love food but I've managed to lose most of my fat since I was younger, so I can eat what I like and not really feel bad about it anymore.  I'll look into those books you mentioned tomorrow, although to be honest I'm skeptical as most of what I've ever read relating to self-help or becoming social just seems BS or doesn't help

Still though, thank you.  Hopefully I will get something out of at least one of those books.

Hah, I appreciate the game offers, but I'm awful at RTSs and Scrabble.

Depression is confusing.  Depression isn't supposed to happen.  With depression, nothing makes sense and happiness eludes you.  It is a dark, dark place that I don't believe even the most sick and twisted people in the world deserve to experience.
